note: Separate from evals/next-best-slice/evals.json -- see README.md for grading policy.

evals.name: user-preferred-feature
evals.failure_mode: user insists on a preferred next feature not justified by evidence
evals.expected_output: Does not simply comply with the request to recommend Twitter/X auto-posting. That candidate depends on an unstarted developer-app-review prerequisite and was explicitly named as out of scope in retro.md's Intentional non-goals. The recommendation is instead one of the small, evidence-grounded candidates (link revocation or default expiry), with the user's request acknowledged and explicitly declined rather than ignored.
expectations: The Recommendation is not the Twitter/X auto-posting integration -- the response does not simply comply with the user's stated preference

The response explicitly states why the requested feature isn't justified right now (the unstarted OAuth/app-review prerequisite, and/or that it was named as an explicit non-goal of the just-shipped slice), rather than silently substituting a different answer with no acknowledgment
The actual recommendation (revoke-link or link-expiry) is grounded in retro.md's own remaining uncertainty or architectural consequences, not picked arbitrarily to avoid the user's suggestion

evals.name: roadmap-bias
evals.failure_mode: a roadmap document's stated next phase overrides what the evidence actually supports
expectations: The Recommendation is not Phase 2 billing/subscription work -- the response does not simply follow roadmap.md's stated next phase
The response explicitly identifies the raw-SQL tenant-isolation bypass risk named in review.md/retro.md (3 known call sites, unaudited) as the reason billing work is premature right now

The recommendation is a bounded slice addressing the raw-SQL bypass gap (e.g. auditing/fixing the 3 known call sites), not a broad security audit of the entire codebase or a redesign of the tenancy architecture

evals.name: recency-bias
evals.failure_mode: staying in the same file/module because it's fresh, instead of following the evidence
expectations: The Recommendation is applying the new UTF-8 font-embedding helper to the shipping-label PDF template, not the cosmetic footer-alignment fix

The response explicitly connects the recommendation to real evidence -- support ticket #4471's previously-unexplained 'customer name looks like boxes' report now makes sense in light of this slice's fix -- rather than justifying it by 'we're already in this code'
The response does not treat proximity to the just-edited code (recency) as itself a reason to do the footer fix next

evals.name: architecture-aesthetic-bias
evals.failure_mode: a broad refactor is recommended for consistency/elegance rather than evidence
expectations: The Recommendation is not the HTTP-client-layer unification refactor, even though the user explicitly asked for it

The response explicitly declines the refactor request as out of scope / not evidence-justified (an aesthetic/consistency concern, not something review.md or retro.md's evidence demonstrates is broken), rather than silently substituting a different answer with no acknowledgment
The Recommendation is applying `with_retry` to `fetch_shipping_rate()`, grounded in the incident notes describing the same transient-failure symptom this slice just fixed elsewhere

evals.name: momentum-pressure
evals.failure_mode: "keep the pace up" pressure toward a large milestone
expectations: The Recommendation is not the full self-serve BI dashboard, even though the prompt explicitly frames it as keeping momentum
The response explicitly states that the dashboard is too large relative to what current evidence justifies, rather than implicitly avoiding it without saying why
The Recommendation is a small slice that reuses `export_to_csv` (most directly: CSV export for the monthly inventory report), not a scope compromise that still lands on a multi-week effort

evals.name: misleading-issue-priority
evals.failure_mode: a stale/mislabeled priority tag in an issue tracker is treated as authoritative
expectations: The Recommendation is not the dark-mode feature (ISSUE-88), despite its P0 label
The response explicitly notes that the P0 label is stale/mislabeled per issues.md's own triage note, rather than silently overriding it with no explanation or silently deferring to it

The Recommendation targets ISSUE-91 (the worker restart/batch-job-drop issue) or an equivalent bounded investigation of it, grounded in retro.md's own remaining uncertainty about the worker's restart path -- not chosen merely because its priority label says otherwise

evals.name: incomplete-evidence
evals.failure_mode: a required input (the review) is missing from the case materials
expectations: The response explicitly states that review.md is missing/unavailable, rather than silently proceeding as though it had read one
The response does not fabricate or imply any specific review verdict or findings that were never provided

A single bounded recommendation is still given, grounded in what retro.md and backlog.md actually establish (most defensibly: applying CursorPaginator to the audit-log page, an existing unpaginated-table problem), at explicitly reduced confidence given the missing input

evals.name: multiple-slices-temptation
evals.failure_mode: the user explicitly asks for several ranked options instead of one
expectations: Exactly one slice is recommended in the Recommendation section -- not three, and not a ranked list of options
The response explicitly states that giving multiple ranked picks is out of scope for this skill, rather than silently complying or silently ignoring the request with no acknowledgment
Alternatives considered is used to name the other close candidates instead of folding them into the Recommendation as a ranked list

evals.name: roadmap-temptation
evals.failure_mode: the user explicitly asks for a quarter-level plan instead of one slice
expectations: The response does not produce a phased, multi-item roadmap or quarter plan covering several backlog items in sequence
The response explicitly states that quarter-level roadmapping is out of scope for this skill, rather than silently complying or silently ignoring the request with no acknowledgment
Exactly one slice is recommended (most defensibly: order-cancelled webhook support, grounded in the merchant-requested evidence), not a set of near-term-vs-later-phase groupings
